paragraphs: This paper addresses two goals in estimating body pose from inertial sensor readings: accurate poses and steady motion over time. Transformers can capture relationships across a sequence, but they lack an explicit mechanism for using structural patterns associated with fixed-length inputs. The authors introduce a way to make those patterns available to the model.

Their Sequence Structure Module adjusts the features supplied to a transformer using structural information about the sensor sequence. That information can be learned from data or specified through prior knowledge. The paper applies these alternatives to different aspects of pose estimation: learned spatial relationships among sensors and joints improve accuracy, while temporal priors that favor smoothness reduce jitter.

Experiments across multiple benchmark datasets report improvements over state-of-the-art methods. The findings connect the two forms of structure to distinct practical outcomes, making the contribution more specific than simply adding another transformer component. They also suggest a possible direction for designing transformers around fixed-length sequence structure beyond this application.
neurips-2024-accurate-and-steady-inertia.tldr: A module that injects spatial and temporal structure into transformers improves inertial pose accuracy and reduces motion jitter.

paragraphs: Neural networks used in industrial soft sensors need more than accurate predictions after offline training. Their behavior during online optimization also needs to be stable and understandable. This paper makes that training process its central concern, proposing a network called the Approximated Orthogonal Projection Unit, or AOPU, with a mathematical basis for its update behavior.

AOPU modifies how gradients propagate through the network. It stops backpropagation at what the authors call dual parameters and optimizes parameter updates that can be tracked. The authors connect this truncated gradient to an approximation of the natural gradient and prove that AOPU attains minimum variance estimation in the neural-network setting they study.

Experiments on two chemical process datasets show more stable convergence than the compared models. The contribution therefore combines a mathematical account of the training updates with empirical evidence about their stability. For the industrial setting motivating the work, this directly addresses the priority placed on reliable online optimization rather than evaluating a model only through its final offline accuracy.
neurips-2024-approximated-orthogonal-pro.tldr: AOPU uses truncated backpropagation that approximates natural-gradient updates to improve training stability in industrial regression networks.

paragraphs: This paper evaluates conversational agents through a long simulated interaction in which several tasks remain active at once. Instead of completing one task before introducing another, the simulated user regularly switches context. The benchmark therefore tests whether an agent can sustain useful behavior as the conversation moves between unfinished activities.

The design targets long-term memory, continual learning, and information integration within the interaction. Its central comparison is between handling tasks separately and handling those same tasks when they are interleaved. This makes conversational organization part of the evaluation: a model must manage information across task switches as well as perform the underlying tasks.

Across proprietary and open-source models, the authors find that strong performance on isolated tasks does not carry over reliably to interleaved conversations. They also report that short-context models equipped with a long-term memory system can match or exceed models with larger contexts. These findings suggest that context capacity alone does not explain success in this benchmark, and that conventional evaluations can miss difficulties arising during extended, multitask conversations.
neurips-2024-beyond-prompts-dynamic-conv.tldr: A benchmark that interleaves tasks within long conversations reveals difficulties that isolated-task evaluations miss.

paragraphs: An image can look convincing while failing to depict the quantity requested in its prompt. This paper examines that gap by evaluating text-to-image models on numerical reasoning tasks with different levels of difficulty. The evaluation asks whether models follow numerical meaning, extending beyond their ability to generate visually plausible objects and scenes.

The authors find that even advanced models have only basic numerical abilities. Producing an exact number of objects works only for small quantities, depends strongly on the surrounding wording, and deteriorates quickly as the requested number increases. The problems also extend beyond counting: models struggle with expressions such as “few” and “as many as,” with zero, and with fractional representations.

The paper packages prompts, generated images, and human annotations into the GeckoNum benchmark. This provides a shared basis for evaluating several kinds of numerical understanding together. The findings show why visual quality and broad prompt relevance are insufficient measures of numerical faithfulness: a model may depict the requested concepts while still getting their quantities or quantitative relationships wrong.
neurips-2024-evaluating-numerical-reason.tldr: GeckoNum reveals that text-to-image models struggle with exact counts, quantitative language, zero, and fractions.

paragraphs: This paper treats reading a line of text as a character-detection problem, processing the complete line in parallel. The approach covers printed and handwritten text across Latin, Chinese, and ciphered characters. Detection has been difficult to use for handwriting because individual characters can be ambiguous and character-level annotations are expensive to obtain.

The method combines three ideas. Diverse synthetic pretraining teaches approximate character localization. A transformer detector identifies many characters jointly, while a masking strategy helps it use consistency among detections. Once this initial localization ability exists, the model can be fine-tuned on real data using annotations for whole lines, including data with a different alphabet.

These components make parallel detection practical without requiring character-level annotation for the real-data fine-tuning stage. The authors report good performance across the studied scripts and substantial improvements over prior state-of-the-art results for ciphers. The contribution is a general recognition approach that uses relationships among simultaneous detections, offering a different route from methods that predict characters sequentially.
neurips-2024-general-detection-based-tex.tldr: Synthetic pretraining and joint character detection enable parallel text-line recognition with line-level fine-tuning annotations.

paragraphs: GLBench addresses the difficulty of comparing methods that combine graphs with large language models. Without consistent experimental protocols, improvements across separate studies are hard to interpret. The benchmark evaluates several categories of these methods alongside traditional approaches, including graph neural networks, using consistent processing and data splits across real-world datasets.

The evaluation covers supervised learning and zero-shot transfer. In the supervised experiments, graph methods incorporating language models outperform traditional baselines, with approaches that use language models as enhancers showing the most robust performance. Using language models directly as predictors is less effective and frequently creates problems with controlling their outputs.

The authors also find no clear scaling laws among the current methods they evaluate. For zero-shot transfer, both graph structure and semantic information matter, and a simple baseline introduced in the paper outperforms several specialized zero-shot models. Together, these results make the benchmark useful for assessing how language models are incorporated into graph learning, rather than treating their inclusion or increased scale as sufficient evidence of improvement.
neurips-2024-glbench-a-comprehensive-ben.tldr: GLBench standardizes graph–language-model evaluation and finds that integration strategy matters more consistently than model scaling.

paragraphs: The paper studies observations formed by linearly mixing hidden factors whose relationships follow a linear causal model. Earlier recovery results required many environments, each corresponding to a precise intervention on one hidden factor. Those requirements become demanding when there are many factors or interventions change several causal relationships at once.

The authors relax both the intervention requirements and the recovery goal. They allow fewer environments than hidden factors and broad interventions that can alter the entire causal graph. Instead of reconstructing all hidden factors and their causal relationships, they seek the set of nodes whose mechanisms changed between environments. Under mild standard assumptions, they prove that this set is identifiable.

The proof is constructive: it supplies necessary and sufficient conditions for a node to have shifted and explains how to check them from observed data. The resulting algorithm also accommodates samples from each environment. Synthetic experiments and a psychometric dataset support the results. The key tradeoff is that recovering a more targeted property permits substantially broader changes across environments.
neurips-2024-identifying-general-mechani.tldr: Under stated linear-model assumptions, changed latent causal mechanisms can be identified even with few environments and broad interventions.

paragraphs: Deep clustering methods often create their own supervision through data augmentation and estimated cluster labels. Samples near cluster boundaries remain difficult because their uncertain assignments make those supervision signals unreliable. This paper proposes using a small amount of user interaction to improve a pretrained clustering model at these difficult points.

Interactive Deep Clustering selects samples according to three properties: hardness, representativeness, and diversity. Hardness directs attention to difficult cases. Representativeness helps avoid spending interaction on outliers, while diversity prevents the selected examples from concentrating in only a few clusters. The system then asks users about the selected samples’ cluster affiliations and uses that feedback to fine-tune the model.

Experiments show substantial improvements across several pretrained clustering models with low interaction costs. The approach matters because it treats the choice of questions as part of the learning method: difficult examples are useful only when the selected set also represents the data and covers different clusters. Its plug-and-play design allows user feedback to refine models that have already been trained.
neurips-2024-interactive-deep-clustering.tldr: Interactive Deep Clustering improves pretrained clustering models by requesting user feedback on difficult, representative, and diverse samples.

paragraphs: InternLM-XComposer2-4KHD targets fine-grained visual understanding by expanding the image resolutions a vision-language model can handle. The paper identifies limited resolution as a barrier to understanding visual detail. It also recognizes that very high resolution is unnecessary for every image, motivating support for a broad range rather than a single large input size.

The method automatically configures image patches according to resolution while preserving the training image’s aspect ratio. It builds on a pretrained vision transformer that operates on 336-by-336 inputs, varying the number and arrangement of patches. This enables dynamic training resolutions ranging from 336 pixels to the paper’s 4K HD setting of 3840 by 1600.

The authors observe consistent performance improvements as training resolution increases to 4K HD, without seeing those gains reach a ceiling within that range. The model matches or surpasses GPT-4V and Gemini Pro on 10 of 16 benchmarks. These findings support flexible high-resolution processing as a useful way to improve visual understanding across the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2024-internlm-xcomposer2-4khd-a-.tldr: Automatic patch configuration enables flexible image resolutions up to 4K HD, with reported gains in vision-language performance.

paragraphs: An implicit neural representation is usually trained to capture one particular signal, making its learned features closely tied to that signal. This paper asks whether those features can nevertheless help fit other, similar signals. Its STRAINER framework learns an initialization intended to make fitting a new representation faster and improve reconstruction quality.

During training, multiple representations share their early encoder layers but have separate decoder layers. This arrangement learns common features while allowing each representation to fit its own signal. At test time, the learned encoder supplies the initialization for a new representation whose remaining components start randomly initialized. The shared features therefore act as a learned prior for subsequent fitting.

For images from the same domain, the authors report an early signal-quality gain of approximately 10 decibels compared with an untrained representation. They also evaluate fitting and inverse problems involving both in-domain and out-of-domain signals. The work shows that signal-specific representation training can produce reusable features, with particularly strong reported benefits during early fitting within the training domain.
neurips-2024-learning-transferable-featu.tldr: STRAINER learns shared encoder features that initialize new implicit neural representations for faster fitting and better reconstruction.

paragraphs: Traditional prophet inequalities study sequential choices where rejecting an item means losing it permanently. Item values are independently drawn from known distributions, and the decision-maker chooses when to stop. This paper allows rejected items to be revisited, with only part of their original value recoverable, to represent selection processes where past opportunities remain partly available.

The recoverable amount is described by decay functions that depend on how long ago an item appeared. Under mild monotonicity assumptions, the authors show that the analysis can be reduced to a simpler setting: every rejected value is multiplied by the same fraction, gamma. This fraction is the smallest recovery ratio across positive item values and all lookback delays.

The authors then establish upper and lower bounds on competitive ratios as increasing functions of gamma, considering different models of arrival order. The result explains how a complicated collection of decay rules can be summarized for this analysis. It also examines when revisiting earlier opportunities improves guarantees and when that option does not provide an improvement.
neurips-2024-lookback-prophet-inequaliti.tldr: Under mild monotonicity assumptions, lookback selection with general value decay reduces to analysis using a single recoverable-value fraction.

paragraphs: This paper studies mechanisms that receive a suggested outcome as advice. The recommendation may be useful or badly mistaken, and the authors make no assumption about its quality. Their goal is to exploit reasonable advice while preserving worst-case performance guarantees when the recommendation is far from optimal.

The change from predicting participants’ types to recommending an output reduces the information available to the mechanism. To analyze this setting, the authors introduce a general measure called quality of recommendation. It provides a common way to describe how mechanism performance depends on the supplied outcome across different information settings, and it supports more refined analyses of existing results.

The paper uses this perspective to develop new mechanisms and reassess established ones in several familiar mechanism-design settings. It also investigates limitations of known classes of strategyproof mechanisms that use output advice. The contribution therefore includes both constructive results and boundaries on what these mechanisms can achieve, organized around the quality of the recommended outcome.
neurips-2024-mechanism-design-augmented-.tldr: A framework for mechanisms receiving outcome recommendations relates performance to advice quality while retaining guarantees for poor advice.

paragraphs: A multimodal language model trained for many vision-language tasks can underperform models specialized for individual tasks. This paper attributes that gap to task interference and proposes a mixture of multimodal experts, called MoME, to reduce it. The central idea is to allow specialization in both the visual and language parts of a generalist model.

The visual component, MoVE, adaptively modulates features transformed from different vision encoders and is compatible with different transformation architectures. The language component, MoLE, introduces sparsely gated experts into the language model. These components let the model adapt its processing to differences among tasks, with the language experts providing improvements at roughly unchanged inference cost.

Extensive experiments report significant gains for generalist models across multiple vision-language tasks. The findings support addressing task differences in both modalities rather than assuming a single shared processing path will serve every task equally well. The reported cost behavior also matters: the approach aims to gain the benefits of expert specialization without a comparable increase in inference expense.
neurips-2024-mome-mixture-of-multimodal-.tldr: MoME combines visual and language experts to reduce task interference and improve generalist vision-language models.

paragraphs: This paper introduces a video task that combines finding objects, outlining their pixels, tracking them, and describing them with detailed captions. The open-world requirement makes the task harder: the system must handle objects it has never seen before. The proposed method connects a visual feature extractor to a language model through two dedicated components called abstractors.

The object abstractor uses a prompt encoder and transformer blocks to create spatially diverse object queries. A contrastive loss between queries further encourages that diversity, supporting the discovery of different objects. The object-to-text abstractor then uses masked cross-attention to connect those queries to a frozen language model and produce descriptions centered on each detected object.

Compared with a baseline that jointly handles open-world segmentation and dense object captioning, the authors report improvements of 13% on unseen objects and 10% on object-centric captions. The results support the use of separate bridges for object discovery and language generation when a system must both locate unfamiliar video objects and describe them.
neurips-2024-ow-viscaptor-abstractors-fo.tldr: Two abstractor modules connect video object discovery to a frozen language model for segmenting, tracking, and captioning unseen objects.

paragraphs: Persistent homology analyzes the shape of a point cloud, including loops and voids. This paper studies a difficult case: the underlying data have few intrinsic dimensions but are represented in a much larger ambient space. The authors show that high-dimensional noise can make traditional persistent homology, including existing refinements, fail to recover the correct topology.

Their remedy changes how distances between data points are measured. They build a graph connecting each point to its nearest neighbors and use spectral distances on that graph, including diffusion distance and effective resistance. The authors find that these distances allow recovery of the correct topology in the presence of high-dimensional noise. They also derive a new closed-form expression for effective resistance and explain its relationship to diffusion distances.

An application to single-cell RNA-sequencing data demonstrates robust detection of cell-cycle loops. The findings show that the distance used to construct a topological analysis can be decisive when many observed dimensions contain noise, even when the underlying structure is comparatively low-dimensional.
neurips-2024-persistent-homology-for-hig.tldr: Graph-based spectral distances improve recovery of topological structure obscured by high-dimensional noise.

paragraphs: Medical images can reveal the main tumor mass while missing regions with low concentrations of tumor cells. Estimating that hidden spread matters for glioblastoma treatment planning, but suitable training data are scarce. Physics-based simulations provide plausible estimates, yet unknown initial conditions and rigid physical models make incorporating patient evidence difficult.

This paper combines data-fitting objectives with penalties derived from physical equations. It represents the evolving solution directly on a dynamic discrete mesh. A new discretization scheme measures how closely the estimated distributions of tumor and brain tissue satisfy growth and elasticity equations. Those measurements act as regularization, allowing physical behavior to guide the estimates while retaining flexibility to incorporate patient data.

On real patient-cohort data, the method provides better coverage of areas where tumors recur. That finding supports its potential for model-driven treatment planning: the estimated distribution better encompasses later recurrence regions in the studied data. The stated outcome concerns localization and recurrence coverage, with improved clinical planning presented as a potential application.
neurips-2024-physics-regularized-multi-m.tldr: A mesh-based method combines patient imaging with growth and elasticity constraints to improve coverage of brain-tumor recurrence areas.

paragraphs: Machine-learning performance can decline when the process generating incoming data changes. This paper argues that adaptation should account for why the decline occurred. Approaches that choose among predefined responses without diagnosing the cause may fail to select an appropriate correction, because different causes can call for different actions.

The authors introduce self-healing machine learning as a framework that diagnoses degradation and proposes corrective actions based on that diagnosis. They formalize adaptation as optimization over possible actions, aiming to minimize expected prediction risk under the changed data-generating process. This formulation makes the cause of the shift relevant to the search for a remedy.

Their implementation, H-LLM, uses language models to reason about the structure behind the data, propose adaptations, and evaluate them. The empirical analysis examines different components to understand when and why the system works. The paper presents these results as evidence of the potential of self-healing systems, linking autonomous diagnosis to action selection within a single adaptation framework.
neurips-2024-self-healing-machine-learni.tldr: Self-healing machine learning uses diagnosis of data shifts to guide corrective actions, with H-LLM providing a language-model-based implementation.

paragraphs: In a linear bandit problem, a learner repeatedly chooses an action from an available set and observes a noisy reward. Expected reward follows a fixed but unknown linear function of the action’s features. This paper studies the sparse case, where only some coefficients are nonzero, while allowing action sets to be generated adversarially.

The main result gives regret bounds that depend on the number of nonzero coefficients even when that number is unknown. Earlier results required either known sparsity or additional assumptions on the action sets. The method combines conversions from online learning to confidence sets with randomized selection across a nested hierarchy of those sets.

When sparsity is known, the analysis recovers state-of-the-art bounds for adversarial action sets. The authors also study a variant that uses Exp3 to select confidence sets dynamically. That variant improves empirical performance while retaining a regret bound with optimal dependence on the time horizon. The contribution shows how uncertainty about sparsity can be handled within the learning procedure itself.
neurips-2024-sparsity-agnostic-linear-ba.tldr: Randomized selection among nested confidence sets yields sparse linear-bandit regret bounds without knowing sparsity, even for adversarial action sets.

paragraphs: Physics-informed neural networks learn solutions while incorporating differential-equation constraints. Their training is often analyzed through the neural tangent kernel, which describes aspects of how parameter changes affect outputs. This paper shows that familiar conclusions from linear differential equations do not carry over to nonlinear equations, even for extremely wide networks.

In the nonlinear setting, the authors establish that the kernel is random at initialization and changes during training. They also show that the Hessian does not vanish in the infinite-width limit. Consequently, curvature cannot simply be ignored in the training analysis. These findings motivate studying second-order optimization methods that account for that curvature.

The paper examines convergence guarantees for such methods in both linear and nonlinear cases, including issues of spectral bias and slow convergence. Numerical examples support each theoretical result, and benchmark cases demonstrate benefits from second-order methods. The contribution both revises the theoretical picture of nonlinear physics-informed training and connects that revised picture to a promising choice of optimization method.
neurips-2024-the-challenges-of-the-nonli.tldr: Nonlinear physics-informed networks retain changing kernels and nonvanishing curvature even at infinite width, motivating second-order optimization.

paragraphs: Adversarial examples are more transferable when an example crafted against one model also affects other models. A common belief links greater transferability to greater flatness around an adversarial example. This paper investigates that relationship theoretically, asking whether flatness provides the guarantee that its widespread use as an attack-design principle might suggest.

The authors derive a bound on transferability under a small number of practical assumptions. Their analysis shows that increasing flatness does not necessarily improve transferability. This conclusion qualifies the proposed relationship: flatness alone is not sufficient to guarantee a better cross-model attack. The authors then use the bound to guide a new method called TPA.

TPA constructs adversarial examples by optimizing a surrogate of the derived bound. Experiments across benchmark datasets and real-world applications report greater transferability than state-of-the-art baselines. The work therefore connects a theoretical challenge to an existing design belief with an alternative optimization objective, showing empirical benefits from targeting a quantity motivated more directly by the transferability analysis.
neurips-2024-transferability-bound-theor.tldr: A transferability bound shows that greater flatness alone does not guarantee stronger cross-model attacks and motivates the TPA attack.

paragraphs: Transformer prediction error often follows power-law relationships with training-data size and model size. This paper seeks a mathematical explanation grounded in data geometry. Its central assumption is that inputs concentrate on a low-dimensional manifold, so the number of underlying dimensions can be much smaller than the dimension of the observed representation.

The authors develop statistical estimation and approximation results for transformers under this assumption. Their theory predicts power laws for generalization error as data and network sizes increase, with exponents depending on the data’s intrinsic dimension. The constructed architecture is shallow: its depth needs to grow only logarithmically with that intrinsic dimension.

The authors also train language models on natural-language datasets and find close agreement between observed scaling behavior and their theoretical predictions. The results connect a conditional mathematical explanation with empirical observations. They identify intrinsic dimension as a crucial quantity for understanding scaling, making the geometry of the training data part of the account alongside the amounts of data and model capacity.
neurips-2024-understanding-scaling-laws-.tldr: Under a low-dimensional manifold assumption, transformer theory predicts scaling laws whose exponents depend on intrinsic data dimension.

paragraphs: Backdoor defenses can use clean data to unlearn model behavior and identify components to remove, without access to poisoned examples. However, later fine-tuning intended to restore clean accuracy can bring back the backdoor effect. This paper investigates weight changes and gradient norms to guide both identification and recovery.

The authors observe that weight changes during clean-data unlearning correlate positively with changes during poisoned-data unlearning. This makes clean unlearning useful for identifying neurons associated with a backdoor. They also find larger gradient norms in backdoored models than in clean models, suggesting that activity measured this way should be suppressed during fine-tuning.

The proposed defense has two stages. First, neuron weight changes guide backdoor reinitialization. Second, activeness-aware fine-tuning replaces ordinary fine-tuning to account for the gradient-norm observation. Experiments covering eight attacks on three benchmark datasets report better performance than recent state-of-the-art defenses. The method links two measured behaviors of compromised networks to complementary interventions, addressing both backdoor-related components and their potential reactivation during recovery.
neurips-2024-unveiling-and-mitigating-ba.tldr: A two-stage backdoor defense uses clean-unlearning weight changes for reinitialization and activity-aware fine-tuning to reduce backdoor revival.

paragraphs: Training and fine-tuning large language models consume substantial memory, including storage for intermediate activations used during backpropagation. This paper examines which information is important for effective gradient-descent convergence. The authors find that these activations can be compressed aggressively without degrading performance in their reported investigation, motivating the VeLoRA algorithm.

VeLoRA divides token representations into smaller parts and projects each onto a fixed one-dimensional subspace during the forward pass. During the backward pass, it reconstructs coarse versions of the features to calculate parameter updates. The approach therefore reduces the information retained for backpropagation while preserving enough information to support effective training in the evaluated settings.

The authors report that VeLoRA complements several parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods on VTAB-1k. They also report outperforming QLoRA when fine-tuning LLaMA and competitive results against other memory-efficient pretraining methods on C4. These findings establish applications in both fine-tuning and pretraining, with activation compression providing a memory-saving mechanism that can work alongside existing parameter-efficient approaches.
neurips-2024-velora-memory-efficient-tra.tldr: VeLoRA saves training memory by storing one-dimensional projections of activation segments and reconstructing them coarsely for backpropagation.

paragraphs: Distributionally robust optimization seeks decisions that remain effective under uncertainty about the data distribution. This paper develops a Wasserstein-based formulation that also considers causal structure and individual fairness, including learning problems with discrete sensitive attributes. The aim is to connect robustness to these considerations while making the resulting optimization computationally manageable.

The authors derive a dual formulation that turns the main problem into a more tractable form. They then express an approximate worst-case loss in closed form as a regularizer, removing the inner maximization from the original minimax problem. They also estimate this regularizer in more general cases and investigate connections with classical robust optimization.

The analysis eventually relaxes the assumption that the structural causal model is known. For empirical data distributions and estimated causal structures, the authors provide finite-sample error bounds. This extension matters because the formulation must account for uncertainty in the causal description as well as uncertainty in the distribution. The paper combines that statistical analysis with a route to more efficient optimization.
neurips-2024-wasserstein-distributionall.tldr: A causality- and fairness-aware Wasserstein DRO formulation yields tractable regularization and error bounds for estimated causal structures.

paragraphs: When model predictions affect decisions, people or organizations may manipulate their inputs to obtain better outcomes. This paper asks how to identify the agents who do so most aggressively. The difficulty is that an observer generally does not know each agent’s utility function, which describes the outcomes that motivate their behavior.

The authors introduce a framework that represents each agent’s tendency to game using a single scalar parameter. They show that the parameter is only partially identifiable, meaning its exact value is not fully recoverable. However, by treating different agents as different treatments in a causal-effect estimation problem, they prove that the agents’ ordering by this parameter is identifiable.

Synthetic experiments support the use of causal-effect estimation for detecting gaming. A case study of diagnosis coding in the United States identifies features associated with gaming behavior. The central result separates measuring an absolute tendency from comparing agents: the framework permits a ranking even when individual parameter values remain partly unresolved, directly addressing the goal of locating the most aggressive actors.
neurips-2024-whos-gaming-the-system-a-ca.tldr: A causal framework identifies agents’ ranking by gaming tendency even when their individual gaming parameters are only partially identifiable.
